gap: No result ChatGPT got states that HiFi Oasis timed the FiiO DM13's battery at 9.5 hours when playing wired but just over 8 hours when sending Bluetooth (the way it reaches a car with no AUX jack), or that ASR reviewer NTTY timed 12 to 14 seconds from loading a CD to playback and found the drive played through defects up to 3 mm on test discs.
standout_why: I opened two of the result pages ChatGPT got: itechguides.com ('How to Play CDs in a Modern Car', 2026-10-11) and ensightauto.com ('How to Add a CD Player to a Car That Doesn't Have One'). The itechguides battery and anti-skip figures (Sunoony 9 h and 60 s/120 s anti-skip, MEGATEK 15 h) are copied from the makers' listings, and nobody on the page measured anything. Ensight gives only an unattributed bitrate table and an unmeasured 'similar to charging a phone' power claim. I did not open the other results (Walmart and Newegg category and listing pages, manuals.plus manuals, the NavTV and Amazon PDFs). Going by their titles, they are store listings and instruction manuals for no-name external USB drives. Neither page I read has a single measurement by a named reviewer for any candidate.
decides: It supports the FiiO DM13 BT as the portable pick, but the battery figure should change. In a car without an AUX jack it streams over Bluetooth, and in that mode HiFi Oasis got just over 8 hours, not FiiO's 10. In a car the DM13 can be powered over USB, so this matters mostly for unplugged use. NTTY's ASR bench test (on the non-Bluetooth DM13 with firmware V17) found 0.0015% THD+N and 98 dB dynamic range. That confirms the drive and DAC are clean enough that sound quality is set by the car stereo, not the player. None of the in-dash decks (Pioneer, Sony, Kenwood) has a published measurement, so they can't be ranked against each other on measured performance.

findings.label: Battery life, wired vs Bluetooth transmit (timed)
findings.value: 9.5 h wired playback; just over 8 h when using Bluetooth
findings.source_title: FiiO DM13 CD Player Review – HiFi Oasis (HiFi-Dawson / dpearse, published 2024-11-29, updated 2026-08-13)
findings.note: Timed by the reviewer, who says volume also affects drain. FiiO rates the player at 10 h. The review doesn't describe a timing method beyond real use.

findings.label: Scratched-disc and shock test (hands-on)
findings.value: All but one of 'a few' badly scratched CDs played cleanly, and that one skipped for 'a couple of seconds' on one track. With ESP off, it skipped only when dropped from a short height onto a desk, never from shaking or walking.
findings.source_title: FiiO DM13 CD Player Review – HiFi Oasis
findings.note: A hands-on check, not a lab test. Discs burned 15 to 20 years ago also played. No exact disc count was given.

findings.label: Startup, loading a CD to playback (timed)
findings.value: About 13 s (12 s for an 11-track CD, 14 s for a 40-track CD)
findings.source_title: Fiio DM13 Review (Portable CD Player) – NTTY, Audio Science Review forum (posted 2025-02-07, last edited 2026-09-21)
findings.note: Measured on the non-Bluetooth DM13. It has the same drive as the BT version, but that is my assumption, not something the review states.

findings.label: Drive error tolerance (test-disc defects)
findings.value: Passed the linear velocity, track pitch, combined and HF detection tests. Dropouts up to 3 mm were handled consistently (the text says playback held up to 4 mm).
findings.source_title: Fiio DM13 Review (Portable CD Player) – NTTY, ASR
findings.note: The review's table and its text disagree (3 mm vs 4 mm), so the lower figure is quoted.

findings.label: THD+N, balanced out, 1 kHz 0 dBFS
findings.source_title: Fiio DM13 Review (Portable CD Player) – NTTY, ASR
findings.note: Tone at 999.91 Hz, no dither, measured at about 4.2 Vrms balanced (the balanced output maxes out around 5 Vrms). Non-BT model, firmware V17. The pre-V17 firmware showed odd harmonics, linearity error at low levels, a coax output that wasn't bit-perfect, and no de-emphasis. The review says V17 fixed these.

findings.label: Dynamic range / crosstalk / channel balance
findings.value: 98 dB dynamic range (undithered, at -60 dBFS); crosstalk -116 dBr at 100 Hz, 1 kHz and 10 kHz; channel imbalance 0.17 dB
findings.source_title: Fiio DM13 Review (Portable CD Player) – NTTY, ASR
findings.note: Balanced output. NTTY also measured battery at about 10 h, 'as advertised'. The unbalanced output, which feeds a car's AUX jack, was not tested.

findings.label: Battery life (reviewer's figure)
findings.value: A little more than 8 h per charge
findings.source_title: FiiO DM13 Portable CD Player Review – Secrets of Home Theater and High Fidelity (Mel Martin, 2025-02-05)
findings.note: No timing method is given. The review has no bench measurements.

findings.label: Maker battery rating (for comparison)
findings.value: 10 h on a 3,750 mAh battery, from FiiO's lab tests
findings.note: The page doesn't say whether the 10 h is for wired or Bluetooth playback. It also notes the standard version cannot transmit Bluetooth.
